The woman is made of flesh, just like man, who is made out of dust. This is revolutionary because you would think men are superior. But the Bible tells us women are made of actual flesh. That's why some believe the writer was a woman. As you read more, you'll find this genius who wrote the Bible first was likely a woman—quite revolutionary.

A man leaves his father and mother and clings to his wife, becoming one flesh. The man and his wife were naked but not ashamed. 

The serpent, more crafty than any other animal, said to the woman, "Did God say you should not eat from any tree in the garden?" The woman replied, "We can eat from most trees, but we must not touch the tree in the middle or die." This is strange because the serpent talks only to the woman and they debate. 

The serpent claimed eating would open their eyes and make them like gods. Seeing the fruit was good for food and appealing, the woman took some and ate, giving some to her husband who also ate. Immediately, their eyes opened, revealing nakedness.

The woman judged for herself that the food was good and ate it by herself, then told her husband to eat as well. They both fell. The real hero of the story is actually the woman.

God called the man, asking where he was. The man said he heard God in the garden and hid because he was naked. 

God asked if he had eaten from the forbidden tree. The man blamed the woman, saying she tricked him into eating. However, at this point, we can expect that God does not kill Adam and Eve; instead, consequences follow.
